title: A line the tree does not place keeps the author's own indentation.
text: `indent.rs`'s own doc says which ones those are: a `switch`, a template region's own text, and every continuation line inside an expression. The first two are rules that have not landed — the `?>` that opens a template region is code and is placed, the text after it is not — and a continuation line is placed by `rule:tooling/fmt-a-list-is-one-line-or-one-item-per-line`, `rule:tooling/fmt-a-broken-call-chain-is-one-call-per-line` or `rule:tooling/fmt-a-broken-operator-chain-is-one-operand-per-line` when it is a part of a broken construct, and otherwise stays the author's under `rule:tooling/fmt-never-reflows`. A comment line is placed with the code below it, so it follows that code's answer. A property hook's block has no node of its own, so its statements are placed one level in from the property's line rather than from the hook's.
